correctness.rationale: For the fixed irreflexive four-node Kripke target r->c and c->t,c->f and any monotone NAE3 incidence source with nonempty clause set, every surjective p-morphism necessarily sends unique root rho to r: sink variables cannot map to r/c by back and clause nodes cannot map r because a sink successor would need image c. Forth then sends every clause to c, variables to t/f; back at each clause requires both colors, exactly monotone NAE3. Conversely every satisfying assignment uniquely defines a surjective forth/back p-morphism, including repeated-variable clauses and isolated variables. Thus the reduction is parsimonious from #NAE3, not incorrectly claimed parsimonious from #SAT. Enumerating a candidate map is polynomial so problem belongs to #P; Creignou-Hermann counting CSP dichotomy yields #P-hardness since NAE3 has six tuples and is not affine. Independent exhaustive map vs satisfying-assignment counts for representative 1..3 variable incidence frames corroborate the bijection. General proof is the explicit forced-level argument.
